title: La Silla star trails
caption: Star trails over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Star trails wheel across the sky above a group of telescopes at ESO's La Silla Observatory. The photograph, credited to F. Char, gathers five of them in one scene.

Beneath the trails sit the ESO 3.6-meter telescope, the Swedish-ESO Submillimeter Telescope, the ESO New Technology Telescope, known as NTT, the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope, plus the smaller ESO 1-meter Schmidt telescope. Together they show the variety of instruments that have been built on this mountain over the years, from optical telescopes of different sizes to a dish designed for submillimeter light.

The trails themselves record Earth's rotation. While the camera collected light, the planet turned, and each star was drawn out into a curve across the sky. The telescopes turn along with the camera, so only the distant stars appear to move.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla. The exposure settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points. Only a long exposure can record their apparent motion as trails.
